title: Rust EDHOC KDF uses wrong info structure (4 elements instead of RFC 9528 3 elements)
description:
## Bug

Rust `edhoc_kdf()` in `crates/oscore/src/edhoc/kdf.rs` builds info as `(length, TH, label, context)` - 4 elements.

RFC 9528 Section 4.1.2 specifies `info = (label, context, length)` - 3 elements. TH should be passed AS context by the caller, not as a separate field.

## File
`/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/oscore/src/edhoc/kdf.rs` lines 20-90

## Fix
Same as Python fix in project-LICHEN-worker6-9xfw:
1. Change signature to `edhoc_kdf(prk, label, context, length)`
2. Change info encoding to `(label, context, length)`
3. Use integer labels (0, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 10) per RFC
4. Update all call sites to pass TH as context where needed

## Blocked by
Must coordinate with C fix and regenerate shared test vectors after all three implementations align.
close_reason: Already fixed: Current code in kdf.rs correctly implements RFC 9528 Section 4.1.2 with 3-element info structure (label, context, length). Function signature is edhoc_kdf(prk, label, context, length), integer labels match RFC Figure 6, and TH is passed as context by callers.
